svg.title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Expanding Delivery
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Cash Before Expanding Delivery; subtitle: Four buckets sum to a $60,000 illustrative launch budget.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are USD allocations in the $60,000 central illustration, inside the canonical $15,000–$100,000 startup range. Allocation shares are 20%, 30%, 20%, and 30%. Applying the same shares to the two endpoints produces complete $15,000 and $100,000 comparison budgets. These are cash allocations, not annual expenses or recognized revenue.; caption: First-deal timing remains 3–12 months. The $18,000 reserve covers 4.5 months at $4,000 monthly cash burn or 0.9 months at $20,000; it does not fund a fully staffed Base pod.; stages: label: Formation and operating setup; value: $12,000 central allocation; 20% of total startup capital.; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Fund entity setup, contract drafting, initial insurance, security configuration, and bookkeeping implementation. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $3,000 and $20,000 respectively.; label: CRM and research infrastructure; value: $18,000 central allocation; 30% of total startup capital.; numeric value: 18000.0; detail: Fund scoped CRM implementation, licensed research inputs, scheduling integration, and initial attribution reporting. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $4,500 and $30,000 respectively.; label: Pilot production and proof; value: $12,000 central allocation; 20% of total startup capital.; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Fund limited specialist assignments, account briefs, messaging assets, and acceptance-ledger testing for a narrow pilot. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $3,000 and $20,000 respectively.; label: Uncommitted cash reserve; value: $18,000 central allocation; 30% of total startup capital.; numeric value: 18000.0; detail: Retain liquid cash for collection delays and essential operating commitments. At the $15,000 and $100,000 endpoints, allocate $4,500 and $30,000 respectively. Reduce commitments or secure more runway if the sales-cycle forecast exceeds available cash.
